summary: A client with no endpoint set finds a daemon started with --socket elsewhere: when nothing answers at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/st3.sock it follows the discovery link the daemon publishes at STATE/run/st3.sock, and a refused socket no daemon holds says the daemon may be listening on another socket

replay.detail: No claim, projection or replay changes.

compatibility.detail: Client only. Endpoint discovery without --endpoint, ST3_ENDPOINT or a configured socket still prefers $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/st3.sock; only when that socket does not accept a connection and the daemon's existing STATE/run/st3.sock link leads to one that does, the client connects there. Daemons already publish that link, so this works with every daemon version that does. The unreachable message adds a hint when the refused socket's readiness lock is held by no daemon.

manual.detail: No operator action is required. A stale socket left at the runtime default stays harmless and can be removed by hand.

recovery.detail: Rolling back is safe: clients use the runtime default alone again.
